tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Appeal filed by GST department against Order of Joint Commissioner, GST, Division Haridwar, dropping SCN ( i.e. order passed in favour of BHEL). Issues in brief: (I) GST ITC disallowed-Rs 14.39 Cr /- & (II) short payment of GST Rs. 16.81 Cr./- due to difference in E way bill and GSTR-3B liability. Total Amount under dispute was Rs. 31.20 Cr. plus applicable interest & penalty. Hearing completed before Ist Appellate Authority, Appeal Order was awaited.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner CGST, Dehradun through Assistant Commissioner CGST Division , Haridwar.
tax_litigation.status: Order passed by Commissioner, CGST(Appeals) in favor of BHEL, quashing the demand raised by the GST department .

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Service Tax demand amounting to Rs. 26.80 Cr. on account of denial of abatement benefit for Industrial or Commercial Construction Services. Case is remanded back by CESTAT, Mumbai for fresh computation of liability, Appeal filed by BHEL have been allowed by way of remand to the original adjudicating authority for conducting de novo adjudication proceedings and for passing a fresh order.
tax_litigation.status: Date of the personal hearing is yet to be decided by the Adjudicating Authority.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Sales Tax Demand amounting to Rs. 99.37 Cr. against disallowance of Sale in course of Import benefit u/s. 5(2) of CST Act, Pending Concessional Forms, ITC disallowed, consequential Interest & Penalty. Appeal Order received in Dec'25, as per which liability reduced to Rs. 1.36 Cr. For balance liability of Rs. 1.36 Cr., settlement under Amensty Scheme has been applied, resulting in final payment of Rs. 0.29 Cr. for closure of the case.
tax_litigation.status: Case closed under Maharashtra Settlement of Arrears of Tax, Interest, Penalty or Late Fee (Payable by Public Sector Undertaking Companies) Act, 2025.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Sales Tax demand amounting to Rs. 44.58 Cr. on account of: 1. Inter-State Sales wrongly disallowed, 2. Turnover of other Mfg. Units treated as local sale & wrongly tax charged on the same. 3. Wrongly Tax charged on Turnover mentioned in WCT TDS certificate while the same was already considered in earlier Years. Appeal filed by Deptt. and pending before Rajasthan Tax Board, Ajmer. Last hearing held on 28.11.2024.
tax_litigation.status: Hearing held on 20.01.2026, however case not yet decided.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Service Tax demand amounting to Rs. 31.55 Cr. on Freight and Insurance Income. Appeal filed by BHEL and pending before CESTAT, Allahabad.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: A Show Cause Notice was issued by Tax Authorities for the financial years 2021-22 to 2023-24, involving an amount of Rs. 586 Cr. based on Books of Accounts and GST Returns. Out of three years, i.r.t. SCN for FY 2021-22, Adjudication has been completed and Demand dropped for an amount of Rs.183.77 Cr. out of Rs. 184.55 Cr. For the balance of Rs.0.78 Cr., an appeal shall be filed before Appellate Authorities. FY 2022-23 & 2023-24 will be taken up in similar way.
tax_litigation.status: Appeal filed for FY 2021-22. For F.Y 2022-23, replies submitted and adjudication under process.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Show Cause Notices issued by Tax Authorities subsequent to Audit of the FY 2019-20 to 2022-23. Total Amount involved is Rs.65.75 Cr. The Company is in the process of filing detailed reply with facts, figures and justification along with required evidences substantiating its tax position before the concerned authority within the prescribed timelines.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner of Central Tax, Mysuru Audit
tax_litigation.status: Adjudication has been completed and demand amounting to Rs. 54.83 Cr. dropped out of total demand of Rs. 65.75 Cr. For the balance demand of Rs.10.92 Cr., an appeal shall be filed before Appellate Authorities.

operating_notes.text: Trade receivables include ₹196 Cr (USD 23 million) from STPG (formerly NEC Sudan) considered good; a provision would cut PBT by ₹176 Cr net of ECL.
19 branches reviewed by branch auditors contributed revenue of ₹7,919 Cr and PBT of ₹174 Cr in Q2FY27.
Consolidated results include JVs BHEL-GE Gas Turbine Services, Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals, Raichur Power Corporation and NTPC-BHEL Power Projects; the company has no subsidiary.

predictions.kpi: EBITDA margin sustained above Q2FY27 level
Inventories drawn down from 30 Sep 2026 level

timeline.summary: BHEL entered into a Licensing Agreement for Transfer of Technology (LAToT) with NSTL-DRDO for GT-IRSS for Naval Vessels
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹12,310.37 Cr (+36.9% YoY), net profit ₹1,290.47 Cr (+155.8% YoY).
Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited’s Board of Directors, led by Dr. Yogesh R Chhabra, recommended a final dividend of ₹1.40 per equity share (₹2 each) on May 4, 2026.
2026-05-28: BHEL fined ₹10.99 lakh by BSE and NSE for board composition non-compliance
BHEL signed a ₹2,000-2,500 Cr contract with Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals Free Zone Enterprise, Nigeria for 8 gas turbine generator packages to be executed within 26 months
2026-06-05: BHEL received a ₹21,000 Cr Notification of Award from MUNPL for 3x800 MW Meja STPP Stage-II EPC package
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹9,300.35 Cr (+23.8% YoY), net profit ₹820.94 Cr (+119.0% YoY).
2026-10-14: BHEL board approved ₹500 Cr capex for Haridwar unit and merger of EMRP and EDN
